Route 5 (block structure): under the K-PANAS order mean within-block r = 0.400 and mean between-block r = -0.007 (gap 0.407) and all 20 items sit with their own block; under the canonical order within = 0.200, between = 0.170, gap = 0.030 -- a 13-fold difference, which refutes the canonical reading outright. Route 1 applied to a published correlation matrix rather than to means: Park et al. (2022) Table 1 gives the complete 20x20 K-PANAS matrix for an independent Korean college sample (N=875); the two 190-entry lower triangles correlate r = 0.968, the largest entry in both matrices is the same cell (published r(C13,C20) = 0.71 vs live r(PANAS13,PANAS20) = 0.72, and r(C16,C20) = 0.65 vs live 0.67), and the globally optimal one-to-one assignment of live items to published items (Hungarian on the 20x20 profile-correlation matrix) is the IDENTITY with 20/20 fixed points -- sum of matched profile r = 19.11 against 0.90 (SD 3.86) for random relabellings, p < 1/20000. public_note: The PANAS was administered in Korean (the Park & Lee, 2016 translation), but neither the PeerJ paper nor its supplements reproduce any Korean wording -- the deposit workbook carries bare column headers PANAS1..PANAS20 and no variable labels -- so the item text shown is the English PANAS adjectives and is not what respondents read. Note that PANAS1..PANAS20 do NOT follow the canonical Watson, Clark & Tellegen (1988) item order: the Korean version runs interested, irritable, distressed, alert, excited, ashamed, upset, inspired, strong, nervous, guilty, determined, scared, attentive, hostile, jittery, enthusiastic, active, proud, afraid, so positive-affect items sit at positions 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 18 and 19. The live data confirms this (mean within-valence correlation 0.40 against 0.00 between valences, versus 0.20 and 0.17 under the canonical order), but the scared/afraid pair (PANAS13/PANAS20) cannot be told apart from the data alone. Only the two endpoints of the 1-5 scale are labelled in the source ('not at all', 'very true'); the middle points are left blank rather than invented

note: Item wording transcribed from the deposit's own Supplement 1, '50 items of the women's health nursing examination in Korean' (Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/PWV6H2, file 13126447, CC0 1.0), which prints the exam verbatim and numbers its items 1-50. data/lee_2025_nursing_exam.py renames the raw .tab columns '1'..'50' to item_01..item_50 (f"item_{int(c):02d}"), a number-preserving rename, so the IRW code is the source column name zero-padded. Deviations from a literal transcript, all deliberate: (1) the instructor's answer key, printed as a bare digit at the end of each stem (sometimes as '답 5' / '정답 2'), was removed from item_text and moved to correct_response; (2) item 44's stem carried an instructor's marginal correction '=> 경성하감이다' after the statement, which was dropped as it was not part of the administered item; (3) item 23's option markers are printed as ➀-➄ in the PDF and were normalised to ①-⑤ to match the other 38 multiple-choice items; (4) line breaks inside stems were closed up (e.g. item 16 '절제술 을' -> '절제술을'). The five alternatives of each multiple-choice item are carried inside item_text, after the stem, because the live resp is a 0/1 score rather than the chosen alternative -- so option_text holds the score labels 'Incorrect'/'Correct' and has no administered counterpart to translate (the option_text_translated column is therefore omitted rather than shipped empty). correct_response is the printed option number (1-5 for items 1-39; for the true/false items 40-50 the exam's own coding of 1=true, 2=false, stated in that section's section_prompt). English in the _translated columns was produced by this project; the deposit publishes no English wording (Dataset 2 gives English topic labels only). key_source=source_published: correct_response is the answer key printed in Supplement 1 itself, not derived from the response data.
public_note: The Korean item and instruction text is transcribed verbatim from the study's own deposited examination paper; the English in the _translated columns was produced by IRW, not by the study authors. The .sav carries NO variable labels (all 49 are None), so the item wording is not in the deposit; it was transcribed verbatim from that form. Base fields hold the administered Spanish; the _translated columns hold the instrument publisher's English BREQ-3 (Markland, Bangor, breq-3.pdf, Oct 2014), matched item-for-item -- the English form has 24 items and its own different numbering, so the pairing was made by content and confirmed by subscale (the Spanish version drops the English introjected item 22, 'I would feel bad about myself if I was not making time to exercise'). Anchors: instrument 0-4 rescaled by the study to 1-5; option_text blank at resp 2/3/4 because the printed Spanish form labels only the endpoints, and the deposit's own five English value labels are an agreement-scale gloss contradicting the paper's stated truth-for-me anchors, so they were NOT shipped. Direction of the coding is settled by the .sav value labels (1='Strongly disagree' ascending) and by the data (intrinsic mean 4.63 vs amotivation 1.37 in recreational runners).
public_note: The BREQ-3's 0-4 response scale was administered here as 1-5, and the two descriptions of its anchors disagree: the study's SPSS deposit labels the five points as an agreement scale while the paper states the instrument's usual 'not true for me' / 'sometimes true for me' / 'very true for me' anchoring; the instrument's anchors are what we ship, and the unlabelled scale points are left blank rather than filled in
